utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning to you all. The Chamber must apologise for having kept you waiting this morning. When we were here, an emergency arose which had nothing to do with this particular case which required immediate attention. We are sorry that you've been kept waiting. Good morning, Madam P-013, if you're used to that name by now. May I remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence which still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic? Oh, Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour, good morning do everyone. I wish to introduce myself to the witness. I am attorney Bulatovic, one of the counsel appearing for Mr. Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, my colleagues have already told you about the manner of examination so I will not waste time doing it again. Madam, yesterday we heard you to say that your son brought you to the hospital sometime in September 1991.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that to the best of your knowledge, your son knew Dr. Bosanac, the head of the hospital. I will ask you whether, with reference to the acquaintance between your son and Dr. Bosanac, you know something more, such as how long they had known each other, where they had met, what kind of an acquaintance it was, and so on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything more apart from what I said. I think he knew her from the time she was appointed head of the hospital, not before that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how they met?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you arrived in the hospital in mid-September or towards the end of September after your house and your garage were destroyed, and that your husband remained. Can you explain to me where your husband remained and why he remained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He remained at home in the cellar. We had a small cellar and he didn't want to go anywhere. He simply stayed behind. He stayed at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Was he alone in that cellar or were there neighbours there with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he was alone in our cellar. But after that, I don't know where he went or where he stayed. For the most part, he stayed in our neighbourhood. That's where he was wounded and, after that, brought to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you say your neighbourhood, could you explain what neighbourhood that is?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: (redacted) I don't know how familiar you are with the place, about ten minutes' walk away from the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And how far is it from your house to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe two kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You say your husband was wounded. Do you know under what circumstances, where and how he was wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was outside, outdoors. A shell landed on the house across the street from our house, and he was wounded in the neck by a piece of shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: At the time of his wounding, was your husband a member of the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that my husband was not in the ZNG. He was wearing civilian clothes. My husband was an invalid, and he was wounded like many other people in Vukovar when a shell landed. Shrapnel would fly everywhere. That's how he was wounded and he was brought to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You say your husband was an invalid. Can you tell me what year your husband was born and when and how he became an invalid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My husband was born in 1950. As a young man he went to work in Austria. He fell from a building. From the age of 25, he was a work invalid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mrs. Tuma?

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you. Just if there are any more detailed questions in this area just to remind about the protective measures that are concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Tuma. I don't think there has been a problem so far.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sure Mr. Bulatovic is aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, Your Honour. Should I put a question which would in any way endanger the protection of the witness's identity, I will ask to go into private session, although I feel there will be no need for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether you were present in the hospital when your husband was brought in there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the hospital, but I was not present when he was brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: How did you find out he had been brought to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody came to tell me that he had been wounded, and after they dressed his wound, he was already in bed. I saw him on the following day, lying there wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What time was it, do you remember, when you were told that your husband has been -- had been brought to hospital and that he had been wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the hour, if he was wounded on the 31st, it might have been on the following day that I learnt he was in hospital, not before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So he was wounded on the 31st of September and you didn't see him on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: But you did see him on the following day. In what ward was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There weren't any wards. It was all in the basement. There were beds, even bunk beds there because there was very little space. There was a patient on the lower bed and he was on the upper bed, above that other patient.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Was this in a hospital room, on the ground floor or in the basement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the atomic shelter under the hospital, under the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many other patients were there with him in that atomic shelter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a lot of patients, a lot of wounded, a lot. I didn't count them so I can't tell you the number but there were very many of them. Somebody was wounded and brought in every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what doctor took care of your husband's injuries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who was looking after him, but I always saw Dr. Ivankovic and Dr. Njavro there. I saw others there from time to time, but the ones I saw most often were Njavro and Ivankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: From the 31st of September which you say was the date when he was wounded until the 20th of November, did your husband get up, get out of bed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He could go to the toilet, but he was always there in that area where they were all in bed, but he could move about and he could go to the toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of your testimony, when you entered the courtroom, you said that your husband's injury was not serious and that he was missing and nothing is known of him to this day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I say that his injuries were slight, because in a month and a half or so he was able to move around, and when they had to go out, all those who were able to walk were able to walk out of the building. Those who were seriously injured, who were in plaster and so on, they couldn't go out by themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you mentioned plaster, if I'm not wrong, when you spoke about Mr. Dosen, you mentioned that he was in a plaster cast. Can you explain what part of his body was a plaster cast?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was his whole leg from the hip downwards. I don't know how the plaster was applied. I didn't apply it. I just saw it, but I can't tell you anything specific about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: The reason I asked this was that it occurred to me in this context to ask you something about your husband. During his stay in hospital, did you visit him, speak with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any consequences arising from the injury to his neck? Any kind -- please wait. For example, was there a speech impairment or was it difficult for him to move his neck or anything else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He just said that he felt dizzy sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't catch the answer. I think I've missed it. I'll ask you again. Has your husband been found?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he has not been found, to this very day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just another question in relation to your husband, to wrap it up. Do you know who brought your husband to the hospital and how?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that a man happened to be driving by when he was there, he put him in this small car called Fica and brought him to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted) I am deliberately not referring to your occupation for obvious reasons. What I want to know is where was this kitchen physically located? Was it inside the hospital? Was it outside the hospital? Or in which specific part of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a makeshift kitchen. It was not a proper kitchen that a hospital should have. It had already been shelled a great deal so it was just a room being used, the ear, nose and throat ward formerly. It was in the old building and this was where we were preparing meals for patients and wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So the kitchen was in the old hospital building, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any physical link between the old building and the new building, in the sense of there being perhaps an underground corridor, or did people have to cross an open area in order to get from one building to the other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an underground corridor that people used to get from one building to the other.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next to the kitchen there was a room where we slept. The supplies were brought in by other people, the supplies were brought into that corridor, into that room. There was no need for me to move about.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that the supplies were brought by other people, were these supplies being brought into the old hospital building or the new one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had to bring it to where the kitchen was, so that's what they did. There were help workers, help workers there, who would bring potatoes and bread or water. It was all brought to that room where we had that makeshift kitchen, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any patients in the old hospital, if I may call it that way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were sick people and wounded all over the place, and that applies to the building that you have mentioned, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who was treating those wounded and until when? I'm referring now to the old hospital building.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the doctors who were at the hospital, nurses and doctors, and there were quite a number of them. Some people died, some people never got well, and some people were there until the fall of Vukovar. Some people may have remained, even after the fall. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So up until the 18th of November, there were still wounded lying around the old hospital, as well as sick people, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were wounded in the hospital up until the 18th, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to show the witness a photograph from one of the OTP exhibit sets. It's from the 65 ter list, 224, the number is 0053-1257, photograph number 3. Your Honour, a correction for the benefit of the transcript, page 9, one line and 2, my question was: Were there any sick people in the old hospital? And the answer only states "in the hospital," as opposed to "the old hospital." I thought that needed clarifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the answer or the witness made clear that there were people everywhere. The import of her evidence as the Chamber understood it included the old building, if that helps you one way or the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have the photograph on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise this building? We talked about this yesterday so in order to not waste any more time on this, this is the hospital building. We heard from our learned friends from the OTP yesterday that this was a photograph that was taken back in 1997, if I'm not mistaken. This means that this is certainly not what the hospital looked like back then. However, do you recognise this building as similar to the building in which you worked in the period that we are discussing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this is the new hospital building.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you indicate in this photograph the rough location of the old hospital building? This is probably -- I don't know -- is it working?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm unable to indicate what you've asked me in this photograph. This is the inner face, so to speak, of the hospital, and the old building is to the left in relation to the main entrance, which is something that I can't see in this photograph. I'm not sure what the angle was that this was taken from. I can't show it to you here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Could you perhaps indicate, using this photograph, where the main entrance is? Could you point at it, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can't. I can't use this photograph. There are steps leading to the main entrance which I can't see in this photograph. It should be the other side of the hospital, at least the way I understand this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we show photograph number 2 from the same set? That may make the situation easier for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have that on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have the new one in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the main entrance here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not sure if the technology is operating. I would like the witness to mark certain points of interest. If that works, I would first of all ask that this photograph be marked at the top of the photograph with the Roman numeral 4.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Am I supposed to mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. At the top of the photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now use the Arabic 1 to mark the main entrance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please place a circle around number 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please place an arrow to mark the direction of the old hospital building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please place the Roman numeral 2 on top of that arrow, or the Arabic 2, rather, and please circle the number 2.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Arabic 2, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Arabic? I'm not sure what you mean. You mean number 2, a -- just plain number 2?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, is the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark any other entrances to the hospital, if you can see any in this photograph? Can you please then explain what sort of entrance we are looking at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the main entrance, the one that I've just marked. I'm about to mark the exit that we used to leave the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please put number 3 there and put a circle around it, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: This arrow in the bottom right corner, what does that show?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the exit. There is a door next to this hall, and this is where you leave the hospital. It's an auxiliary exit and it leads into the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I am afraid that we have misunderstood each other. In my photograph, the one that you've marked, I have an arrow in the lower right corner. Did you place that arrow there and what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me about the whereabouts of the old hospital building. It was to the left, from the entrance to the main building, so to the left there was the old building. Used to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I understand that and you placed the number 2 there, above that arrow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Just below that, there is an arrow on my scene in the lower left corner. So I want to know what that means?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the main entrance to the hospital yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please use number 4 to mark that and circle it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: This building or entrance that you now marked by using number 4, what is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the reception, or the emergency ward. I think the emergency ward was on that side.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to these two entrances to the hospital that you marked, were there any other entrances to the hospital? If so, can we see them in this photograph and can you please mark them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where I put number 3, in peace time, this was a ward where the sick and wounded would be brought into the emergency ward in an ambulance usually. That was the surgery ward.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that in addition to these two main entrances that you marked with 1 and 3, there was no other entrance to the hospital building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You talked about the red cross signs that were placed to mark the hospital off. There is one thing that I'm still not clear about, although my learned friends have asked you about this. Where exactly were those signs positioned? Before that, I would like to ask you the following. This is a photograph of the hospital building that was taken in 1997. Do you remember whether the hospital roof, and I'm now talking about the new building, even before the armed clashes in Vukovar in 1991, looked like this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, can you please describe what the roof looked like, the colour and everything else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Unfortunately whenever I went to the hospital, I didn't look at the roof. If I was sick and I had to go, I went to the hospital but I didn't look at the roof, and I can hardly describe it for you as a consequence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You told me that you would go to the hospital whenever you were sick. My question is: At any time during 1991 and 1990, were you in fact treated in the hospital as a patient? If so, why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Back in 1989, I underwent surgery in the Vukovar Hospital. It was a stomach surgery.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: To go back to the red cross markings, you said that on the old hospital building, there was a Red Cross flag; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the old hospital building -- I mean, perhaps I wouldn't even look at it, but when I was coming to the hospital, you could see it, when I was entering the hospital, when my son would bring me, then that first section of the hospital next to the street, there was a sheet, a piece of fabric, a flag, bearing the markings of the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me how big the flag was and where was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was quite big and it was located on the roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You talked about two red cross markings that were located in the courtyard. This photograph that is still on the screen in front of you, is it possible on the photograph to indicate the place in the courtyard where these two red cross markings were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a tree there, but it would be here somewhere, between the old and the new building.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark that place with a number 5?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Were both of the signs there? And if so, how far apart were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how far apart they were, but they were placed at a distance from each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And where was the other sign placed? Can you please indicate that on the photograph, if you can? And can you mark it with the number 6?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement of the 18th of July 1995, you mention, and you also said that here, that there was no water in the hospital. There they said that you had to get the water from the well which was across from the hospital. Can you show the place where the well was on this photograph, the well from which you got water, the one that was across from the hospital? If possible, please mark it with the number 7.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot do that because it was a bit lower down, next to a house, a bit closer to the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: How far from the hospital was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Maybe some 200 metres. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: According to what you said, you were in the hospital from mid to late September until the 20th of November 1991, and in your statement -- I'm referring to your statement again, the statement that you gave on the 18th of July 1995, that you got water from the firefighters. You said also that whoever left the hospital would be killed and that there was also some doubt about where -- whether there were any people in the hospital who provided information about what was happening in the hospital to somebody on the outside. You said that there were such rumours. I'm interested to know who was it who spread these stories. Is there anybody you can tell us about in the hospital from whom you heard such stories?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The firefighters were getting killed when they went to get water, and, as I stated earlier, and I'm stating it again, there were -- there was talk that there were people inside the hospital who would tip off when they went to get the water so that a shell would be launched or fired at that place. But I don't know who these people were. I cannot tell you something that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you spent so much time in the hospital. When you came to the hospital, were there any people there that you knew from before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very few. I used to -- I knew one woman who worked in the kitchen. Her I knew from before. But the people that I met there and got to know there, that was such a short period so that after such a long time I really cannot remember their names anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, can you tell me, then, how these rumours are spread, if people don't know each other, if they don't spend time in each other's company? How are these stories spread then about people providing information to the outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I spent most of the time in that room where I was, and when there was talk about something like that, somebody would say something, somebody would say something else. I mean, my ears were not sealed shut. I did hear all of those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that there were stories that there was a radio that was being used to tip off information. Did you see any of those people who were in the hospital, the wounded or anybody else, that were using a radio?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that there were stories about Dr. Ivankovic having a radio.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what people said, but I didn't see it. I cannot say it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that a Croat wounded man wanted to kill Dr. Ivankovic but he was prevented from doing that by Dr. Njavro. What I'm interested in is, how did he want to kill him? What happened? And how did Dr. Njavro prevent him from doing what he intended to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came to visit somebody who was wounded and I was just passing by at that moment and I happened to hear that, and he started to shout at Dr. Ivankovic, "What are you doing here, you Serb?" It was something like that. Don't take it literally. But up until that moment, I didn't even know that Dr. Ivankovic was a Serb and he kind of tried to -- went towards him, but Dr. Njavro happened to be there and he took the soldier aside. Of course later I don't know what happened. I mean, I wasn't standing there. I was just passing by.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that Dr. Njavro took the soldier aside, meaning that the person who came to visit someone was wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most probably he was wearing a uniform, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did he have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: We talked about your work there. I'm interested in another thing. Do you have information, based on your work there, how many meals were prepared in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many meals were prepared. I can give you the quantities. We had two enormous pots or caldrons but -- no, they were pots. It wasn't enough for each person or each patient to eat his fill. It was just enough so that people could survive. There wasn't enough food so it wasn't really possible to make large quantities of food for everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a dining room in the hospital? How did people eat the meals that were being prepared in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The food was distributed to wherever people were lying down. It was food like soup or stew. It was not distributed in a dining-room. It wasn't possible to set something up like that in a small space.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And the people who worked in the hospital, the doctors, the nurses, the staff, did they eat in the same way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not treated any better, because, as I said, there wasn't enough food.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who actually took the food in the way you described to the hospital director, Dr. Bosanac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever take food to her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever, on any occasion, for any reason, go to Dr. Bosanac's office or hospital room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever, during your stay at the hospital, talk to her, in view of the fact that you came to the hospital on the recommendation of your son?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never talked to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you if you know whether there was a telephone line at the hospital, and, if yes, did you -- do you know where this telephone was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see it and I don't know. If it did exist, it could only be in the office of the hospital director, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: We heard from you that you heard that there were stories, I mean - and this is a little bit different in your statement, but we will come to that later - stories about this soldier called Sasa, and you said that this soldier, Sasa, called General Raseta, and you described that conversation. I would like to know when and how you found out that there was a soldier called Sasa at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found out about it in the same way that I found out about anything else in the hospital. People who moved around the hospital perhaps would come to the kitchen where we were. There would be talk. You had to talk about something. And amongst other things, I heard, as I said, that there was a Serbian soldier lying in the hospital and that somebody, one of the superiors in the hospital, told him to call this General Raseta and that he, as a Serb soldier, should ask that the hospital is not shelled. This is what I said yesterday, and this is what I'm saying again today.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see this soldier, Sasa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't go to see that soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear, was this a soldier of the Yugoslav People's Army or a Chetnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that he was a regular soldier of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear, in the talks that went on, how the soldier was wounded and how did he come to be brought to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you maybe hear if there were any other JNA soldiers who were brought together with this soldier named Sasa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear where this soldier was accommodated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said that he had his own separate room.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: This information that he had a separate room, did you comment about that with anyone? Was there a particular reason for that? Was there any comment that you heard or made?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear any comments to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Compared to the -- or in relation to the time when you came to the hospital, when was it that you heard about this soldier's conversation with General Raseta? Was it two days after you came to the hospital, ten days, a month after you came to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was already in late -- I don't know but I was probably at the hospital for a month already. It was maybe sometime in October, but I don't know when.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you heard in the hospital that some of the hospital officials or senior staff had asked the soldier to speak with General Raseta. While talking with the people who conveyed this information to you, did you find out who Mr. Raseta was, where he was, what he was doing? What would be the reason to call him? What was his significance so that this soldier would have to call him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear any talk about that. We didn't talk about what was the role of this Mr. Raseta.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: During your stay at the hospital, did you ever hear General Raseta's name mentioned in any other context other than in the context of this soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In your evidence, as well as in the statement that you gave, you often talk about Chetniks and the Yugoslav People's Army, these two terms, Chetniks and the JNA. What I'm interested in is, how did you differentiate between Chetniks and the JNA, if you did make a distinction at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Chetniks that I saw, that's what we called them, and we called them that because they wore beards. They were the ones singing that song.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: The song they were singing, the one you mentioned here for the first time yesterday, when did you hear it for the first time and saw this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 20th, when we were already outside in the courtyard, and when we were told to go to the main entrance of the hospital and out into the street, and that there were buses there that would take us somewhere, a large group of these men wearing beards and carrying a black flag with a skull --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. That wasn't my question. My question was, was this on the 20th or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the 20th of November at about noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And before that, before the 20th of November, at about noon, did you ever see these men, as you described them, wearing beards, carrying a black flag?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Men like them were around that morning, inside the hospital. I mean men with beards.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can understand, this was all on the 20th of November?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Until you arrived in the hospital in mid-September or late September 1991, had you seen these men around your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You say that you went out into the courtyard occasionally. Did you see such men as you described them when you went out around the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: How long have you lived in Vukovar? How long had you lived in Vukovar prior to the 20th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 30 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You worked at a job where many people passed through during those 30 years you probably got to know a lot of people. You knew quite a few people in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I will now mention some dozen names to you. Please just tell me whether you had heard of those people. I will mention whether you knew any of them personally. And if you did, what you knew about them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mrs. Tuma?

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I don't know what kind of names the Defence has in mind here but there could be a name specifically that could be related to the witness. I'm just thinking about the protective measures and I suppose the Defence know the answer of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic will obviously take that into account. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these are not people who have any private link or at least I don't think so, that might threaten the identity of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Does the name Ivica Arbanas ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's because I had no knowledge. This is something quite new. To avoid any future problems that might possibly arise, I will ask to go into private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think a wise move, Mr. Bulatovic. Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke yesterday about your son. You said that he was a member of the ZNG, a member of that particular unit. What I want to know is, can you tell me what sort of a unit that was? After all, your son was a member and your husband was a sympathiser. What sort of a unit was that? Who set it up? Were they armed and to what extent? Who provided their equipment, their weapons, their ammunition, their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mrs. Tuma?

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. At least my ears haven't heard that she has said that her husband was a sympathiser to the ZNG.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Nor have mine, Mr. Bulatovic. Is there some particular reference in the transcript you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there was an omission that I made. I wish to say now, additionally, that I draw on the statement given by the witness on the 18th of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, you'd have to --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which says more than this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll try to phrase the question without mentioning any of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What do you know, Witness, about the ZNG as a unit, as a military formation, in view of the fact that your son was a member?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You say your son was supposed to do his military service in the JNA and asked for this to be postponed for four years. In the meantime he joined the ZNG. What I want to know is, do you know whether he was trained in order to join this unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: No, he wasn't trained? Or no, you don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there was a Crisis Staff at the hospital, so-called Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You never heard anything about it, about meetings being held? The hospital was being shelled after all, there was an armed conflict afoot, and people were being killed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You explained some discrepancies between your statement -- your testimony and the statement you gave back in 1995, and then what you stated in your interview with the OTP when you came to the Tribunal. These discrepancies concerned certain dates. I'm not asking you any questions about those because my colleagues have sufficiently exhausted the subject. But what I want to know about is the person known as Martin Dosen. You said a while ago that he had a plaster cast from hip down all along his left or right leg, I can't remember specifically. What I want to know is, before this event that you spoke about, you weren't sure whether it was the 19th or the 20th, you said that you had known Mr. Dosen from before. Why was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him by sight, and that was why I recognised him when he was being carried out on a stretcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know what Mr. Dosen's occupation was before this, before he arrived at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know his wife?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: During your stay at the hospital, did you perhaps meet her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who his wife is at all? Or was he married?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Am I to take it this as, "No, he wasn't married," or "No, I don't know anything about last wife"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know Martin Dosen's wife. That's what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You saw that he was carried out of the hospital and dropped from the stretcher, as well as kicked while he was on the ground. Is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was dropped off the stretcher and then they kicked him with their boots.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Is this taking place outside the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of this is happening at the exit that we used to leave the building, the auxiliary exit, as it were. It was midway down the path to the buses waiting there outside the hospital exit, between the exit and the buses, midway down that path or thereabouts. That's where he was dropped from the stretcher and kicked.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can we please have that photograph again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic, I've got to give you some bad news, news that I suspect no one of us was aware of about there new technical system and I've been told about it in the last quarter of an hour. Apparently after a time, if the document isn't photographed and saved, the markings are lost. So that when we resume after the break, it will be necessary to have the witness remark the photograph, and then if you want it tendered, to tender it so that it can be saved before the markings are lost. I'm sorry to give you the bad news but I hope all counsel will take note of that as we get used to this new technical system. But I think that brings us to a convenient point now for the first break, which will need to be half an hour because there have been a number of redactions to avoid identifying information. So we will resume at 20 past 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are we in public session?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic, I wonder whether we can immediately sort out that marking of the exhibit before you proceed. Madam, you have in front of you the photograph which you marked earlier. Do you see it on your screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm afraid I must ask to you mark the photograph again. Sorry to ask you to do this. Would you be able to put at the top of the photograph a Roman 4, as you did before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can you indicate with a number 1, an ordinary number 1, the main entrance to the hospital, to the main building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you put a circle around that, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you indicate with a number -- an arrow the direction of the old building? You've told us it's not on the photograph but if you could indicate the direction of where the old building was located, with an arrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you put a number 2 in a circle by that arrow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you mentioned that there was an auxiliary exit which in peace time was used as the ambulance entry. Could you put a number 3 where that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you mentioned that there is an entrance or reception area and the emergency ward. If you could put a number 4 in that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. I think they were all the markings, were they, Mr. Bulatovic? Oh, I missed two more, number 5. You did mention that in the courtyard there were two red cross signs. Could you put a number 5 where they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And you did mention that on the roof of a building there was another red cross sign. Can you indicate with a number 6 where that building was, if it's shown on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You did indicate on the photograph earlier a position that you numbered as 6. Mr. Bulatovic was asking you at that time if you would indicate where that other red cross sign was. Are you able to help us by making that marking again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Which number should I use?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Six.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Perhaps we should clarify: Is that a sign that was on the ground or is that a sign that was on the roof of a building? Can you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The sign that was on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. Now, Mr. Bulatovic, have I covered all your ground again?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, it is. This is everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Just let's go back to number 5. Is this also the red cross sign that was on the ground or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic, do you wish to tender that as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But first I would like to ask the witness something else, if she could please use an arrow and mark it as number 7, to mark the direction of the building bearing a red cross flag.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you put a number 7 in a circle by that one, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that all, Mr. Bulatovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe so, Your Honour. I move that this marked photograph be accepted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. It will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 55, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We learn, every day, Mr. Bulatovic, about the wonders of modern technology. Thank you for going through that again, Madam. Now, you have further questions, Mr. Bulatovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: If we could please go back to the 20th, you spoke about the fact that there were soldiers in the hospital sending women to the right and men to the left, separating them, if I understand you correctly. Please correct me if I'm wrong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a soldier standing at the exit. I went to the right and my husband went to the left, as well as all the other men.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You went to the right, as all the other women, and all the men to the left? Was that the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we use this photograph that we still have on our screens that has been admitted already? So therefore I think we might need a new photograph for the witness to mark a number of points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're correct, I believe. Mr. Bulatovic. We'll just make sure that this has now been electronically saved, and when that has been accomplished we will then put up the original, unmarked photograph again for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You still have the same photograph in front of you, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now please use this technology, use the pen to mark the spot where you left the hospital and the direction you went after you left the hospital? I'm referring to the main entrance.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please trace the whole path that you took, with a line and place an arrow to mark the direction you were moving in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please place a number 1 there and put a circle around it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please use this photograph and draw or mark the direction in which the men went to the left and place number 2 there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: How long did all of this take? How long did it take for you to leave this position marked as number 1 until you reached the end of the arrow, as it were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It started at 7.00 in the morning and went on until about 11.00 a.m. That's how long we were standing in this place, in this spot marked as 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you move from that spot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. For the most part we stood there in a group.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: How many women were there in the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A lot. A lot of people, women and children, a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you give me an approximate number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Not even approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Mr. Sljivancanin. You said you had seen him. On this photograph, can you put a number 3 to mark the spot where you saw him, if this is visible on the map? Where was he talking to this representative of the ICRC or the European Community or whatever it was and we'll establish that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: On this photograph, now that we are dealing with this, to avoid any future technical problems, could the witness put a number 4 to mark the place where the buses were, in which the women and children entered into, including herself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark it with 4 and a circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can the witness mark with a number 5 the place where the buses were on to which the men were loaded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic, I'm asked if you would just pause for a little while, while some technical adjustment is being made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic, I'm going to have to do again what you've just done. Hopefully, the snag has been overcome. Madam, on this photograph in front of you, would you please mark again the direction taken by the women and children as they left the main building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And could you put a number 1 in a circle against that, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you would now mark the direction taken by the men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And could you put a number 2 in a circle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you mark with a number 3 the position where you said you saw Mr. Sljivancanin and a man in a white coat? Hello.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise, on my screen it's been lost again. It's disappeared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And on mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We try again, Mr. Bulatovic. If this fails, I think we will have a break while the technicians come to the bottom of it. But we will try once again. Madam, I'm sorry, but would you mind marking once again the direction you took, and the women and children, as you left the main building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you put a number 1 in a circle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And now could you mark the direction the men took?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And number 2 in a circle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you mark with number 3 the position where you said you saw Mr. Sljivancanin and a man in a white coat or clothing as they talked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now could you mark with a number 4 where the buses were that the women and children went to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. Are there more positions that you want, Mr. Bulatovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes. We marked with 5 the place where the buses were that took the men away.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before I tender this photograph into evidence, I would like the witness to answer one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Position number 5, representing the buses, were these buses in the street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the courtyard of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit number 56.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will just wait to be sure, Mr. Bulatovic. Success! Mrs. Tuma?

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: My apologies but my co-counsel here he just checked concerning Exhibit 55 to see if we did have still the markings on that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's on screen and will be retrieved during the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The absence of that was what alerted the court officer to a continuing problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But it is there and it will be retrieved during the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Now that we are talking about this topic, can the witness say whether these buses that took away the men, what they were like? Can the witness describe them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the buses that took us away, both the men and the women, were olive-grey.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any information as to where these buses were going, the ones that took you away and the ones that took the men away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to the conversation between the man in white and Mr. Sljivancanin, which took place in the spot which you marked with a number 3 on that photograph. Tell us, what time was it? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was early in the morning. It was right away. I said we came out between 6.30 and 7.00 and when we had all come outside and were standing there in the morning, that's when this conversation took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did this conversation take place before the order to separate or after?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had already been separated, because the official in the white coat, who was from the international community, demanded to know the names of the men who had been separated off. He insisted that a list be made of the names of all those men.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Will you tell me how long this conversation lasted, the one between the man in white and Mr. Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was quite a spirited conversation but it didn't last long.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: How far were you from where they were standing as they were having this acrimonious conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About three metres behind them, very close up.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps remember whether there was anyone else there with them as they talked, Mr. Sljivancanin and the man in white?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may have been someone but I'm not certain. There may have been another soldier. When I try to think back I still hear their conversation in my head as it were, and, yes, when I think twice about it, there may have been another soldier there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps see an interpreter interpreting their conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There had to be an interpreter. I wasn't able to understand what the man in white was saying, but I did understand what Mr. Sljivancanin was saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that you assume that an interpreter was there? Do you in fact remember that there was one or do you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There had to be one. Otherwise, I would not have understood, since I did not speak English. He made an explicit demand that a list be drawn up of the wounded and all the other men.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So you didn't hear this from the man in white? You heard this from an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I certainly heard it from someone, these words that were being interpreted and that there was a demand being made to draw up a list.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if it was a male or a female interpreter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What exactly did you hear Mr. Sljivancanin say? Can you repeat the very words for us, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said, "Sir, this is my country. Sir, there is a war going on here. I am the one giving orders here. When I come to your country, I will behave as you expect me to. Therefore, you should behave in the same way."

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps hear that Mr. Sljivancanin mentioned the fact that a lot of his own young soldiers had been killed in that spot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He did say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you had read a great deal of things about these people that I've asked you about while reading Major Sljivancanin's book, if I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me the name of that book and when exactly did you read the book?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The book is called, "This is my country," and I read it perhaps about three months before I arrived here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You often mentioned the JNA shelling you. Let me ask you this: Did your late husband do his regular military service with the JNA? Is this something that you know about, in view of the fact that you said he was a disabled retiree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain what your view of the JNA was? What was your experience of the JNA? What was this JNA? What exactly were they doing? Your personal position on this, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the outset, I saw the JNA as a peacekeeping presence of sorts, but later on they sided clearly with the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you perhaps take these two terms one at a time? At the outset and then later on. Can you please specify, in terms of a time line, when you drew this line of division between the before and the after?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the beginning was sometime in May or June. Borovo Naselje was being targeted from Borovo Selo. The army decided to step in. I mean the JNA when I say "the army."

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know why the army stepped in and who the measures were being taken against?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two parties involved, the army was not fighting itself. There was the ZNG on the one hand, and the army on the other. There was firing from Borovo Selo quite early on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You just mentioned "the Guards." Who exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the Croatian soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that at this time, in May, the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia still existed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps, but I don't remember all the dates when independence was declared and when Slovenia and Croatia split off. I no longer remember the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who Mr. Stipe Mesic was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know he's now president of Croatia. I don't know what he did at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Back in 1991, during this period of time that you are referring to, do you know what Mr. Stipe Mesic's role was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Was he a Croat, an ethnic Croat, or still is, for that matter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't even know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, or, rather, what would your reaction be if I told you that at this time Stipe Mesic was president of the Presidency of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After Comrade Tito, I was not aware of any one of the presidents, nor was I aware of any individual name.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You refer to the Guards. You probably mean the ZNG, the National Guards Corps, don't you? Could you please clarify, if you can, what was the ethnic makeup of the National Guards Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I have to tell you about the ethnic makeup of the town of Vukovar itself. It was mixed, very mixed. There was a large number of mixed marriages; those in fact prevailed. Therefore, National Guards Corps, too, was joined by people who were defending their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I still don't have an answer to my question. Let me try to rephrase that. Were there any Serb members in the ZNG, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. There were. There were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many specifically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't keep count, and I can't know how many, but I'm sure that there were some.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many brigades or units the National Guards Corps in Vukovar comprised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, you refer to a unit that you called the 204th Brigade. What do you know about that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Who told you about its existence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was once we were no longer in Vukovar that somebody mentioned it. There was a letter I received stating that my son had been a member of the 204th Brigade and that's the extent of my knowledge about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember what sort of a letter it was, who you received it from, or why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- I'm not sure what to call it. A certificate, perhaps. It was something that I needed to exercise my rights earned in the homeland war.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: A while ago, you said the only president that you had ever been aware of was Comrade Tito, as you called him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What are your feelings about those times when he was president?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My feelings are very positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Who, then, were the National Guards defending from, if the army facing them was a Yugoslav army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me about the late Comrade Tito. I told you how I felt about those times. What you're asking me now, why the guards were defending and who they were defending from, is not a question that I should be answering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mrs. Tuma?

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Yes, referring to yesterday, those questions are speculative for the witness's point of view, I would say so, and it's also a military question and she already stated yesterday that those matters she is not so well aware of or having any deep knowledge about. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That may be so, but Mr. Bulatovic is entitled to explore them. Carry on, Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Since we are talking about these times, let me ask you something else. Have you ever been heard the term "Ustasha"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When was that and can you please explain? Perhaps I know the meaning of the term but maybe the Trial Chamber are not aware of it. What did this term mean and when did this term Ustasha first come about, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when the term was first used.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Who were Ustasha?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the last war, there were no Ustasha. That's what people called them. That's what people called each other, the Croats called the Serbs Chetniks and, vice versa, the Serbs called the Croats Ustasha. But those were no accurate terms and they didn't apply to the last war, the war in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: That would imply that there were no Chetniks and no Ustasha in the last war, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were soldiers who were fighting, but the term is erroneous, at least in my understanding. However, people obviously chose to use that term.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something. Are you familiar with the ethnic makeup of the JNA, of their units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any Muslims in the JNA in one of their units? Did you hear anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure if you're asking me about before the war or if you're asking me about 1991. Either way, the answer is still I don't know anything about its ethnic makeup.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, who and why opened fire on the JNA units and killed young JNA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bulatovic, that is a question that Mrs. Tuma's objection really does apply to. How can this witness answer that unless she was there and saw fire opened? So after a long delay, I think you've crossed the line Mrs. Tuma was drawing much earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept that, Your Honour. You are entirely right. Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: During your testimony, a lot has been said about the statement you gave in July 1995. There are some things that I'm still not clear about, and with the Court's permission I will need to ask you a few questions in order to obtain clarification. Where did you give this statement dated July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Pula.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many people were present on behalf of the party taking the statement when you were giving your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: The same day you gave the statement, did you also sign the statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I most probably did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you or did you just most probably sign it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What about after that interview? Did you ever talk to those same two persons who took your statement in 1995 again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Was this statement taken from you so that you talked and this was dictated or what was the method by which the statement was taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked and one of them interpreted what I was saying to the other one who was sitting there and typing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So the other one was typing what the first one was interpreting to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In what language did you make your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
